part.text: Now I understand the bug. In `lookup`, a zero-length query interval `[t, t)` fails the `overlaps` clip checks (Joda's `overlaps` returns false when one interval is zero-length and shares its start instant), so the timeline holder containing `t` is returned with its full unclipped interval — matching all data after `t`. I'll fix `lookup` to treat zero-length query intervals as matching nothing, and add the same guard to `isOvershadowed`, which has an identical `overlaps`-based issue (line 477).

The fix is complete and validated.

**Changes** — `processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/timeline/VersionedIntervalTimeline.java`:

1. `lookup()` (VersionedIntervalTimeline.java:738): a zero-length query interval `[t, t)` now returns an empty result immediately. Previously it fell through the loop (holders containing `t` were included) but the `interval.overlaps(lastEntry.getInterval())` clip checks returned false — Joda's `overlaps` excludes a zero-length interval sharing its start instant — so the holder was returned unclipped, matching all data after `t`.

2. `isOvershadowed()` (VersionedIntervalTimeline.java:462): added the same zero-length guard, since its `lower.overlaps(interval)` check has the identical flaw (a zero-length interval represents an empty set and cannot be overshadowed).
